idiom_name: Atomics.compareExchange over SharedArrayBuffer, typed via lib ES2017.SharedMemory
implementation_notes: TypeScript changes nothing at runtime, so the realization is the JavaScript one: a bounded index ring over a SharedArrayBuffer whose words are manipulated with Atomics, with types supplied by the ES2017.SharedMemory lib (the tsconfig lib table lists Atomics and SharedArrayBuffer under ES2017; ESNext also works). Type-safety stops at the ring boundary - the buffer is numeric, so objects travel as indices or handles rather than references - and waiting must happen in a worker because Atomics.wait throws on the main thread (or use waitAsync). As in JavaScript, postMessage/MessageChannel is the idiomatic replacement for hand-off that does not need shared memory; keep the ring for traffic that must bypass the event loop.
pitfalls: Without lib ES2017.SharedMemory (or later) in tsconfig, Atomics and SharedArrayBuffer do not type-check at all.
Atomics.wait is unavailable on the main thread; move the consumer into a worker or use Atomics.waitAsync.
SharedArrayBuffer requires cross-origin isolation in browsers, so the same code cannot silently run as an ordinary page script.
